reason: B is the better proposal because Y2O3 oxide-dispersion strengthening is physically credible in a BCC refractory alloy at 1273 K and can be tested with composition- and processing-matched controls. A’s central premise is poorly grounded: adding a few atomic percent Al to TiVNbTa is unlikely to create coherent L12 precipitates in a BCC refractory matrix, and its cited evidence concerns mainly Ni-rich FCC/L12 systems or B2 precipitates rather than TiVNbTa.
